abstract: Cystic echinococcosis is a zoonotic parasitic disease caused by infection with Echinococcus granulosus. Progressive cyst growth can compress host tissues and elicit immune responses. Characterizing the cellular composition and lineage differentiation of E. granulosus protoscoleces may provide insight into the regulation of parasite proliferation and development and facilitate the identification of potential intervention targets. We generated a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of E. granulosus and identified six major cell populations: Germinative cell, Muscle, Neuron, Storage, Tegument,and Cilium. Germinative cells were heterogeneous: some retained an undifferentiated transcriptional profile, whereas others expressed genes associated with differentiated cell types, consistent with the initiation of lineage-associated programs. RNA velocity analysis suggested four potential trajectories, one involving transitions within the undifferentiated population that may contribute to self-renewal and homeostasis, and three showing trends toward distinct lineage-associated subpopulations. A p53 homolog and threonine dehydrogenase tdh were identified as candidate developmental key genes that may contribute to larval growth and development. This study provides a single-cell atlas of E. granulosus protoscoleces and identifies key candidate genes involved in larval development, providing a foundation for future functional studies and the exploration of potential anthelmintic targets.
